articles.title_zh: Two skulls likely belonging to enslaved people returned to Brazil after Harvard used them in eugenics studies
facts_zh: Remains believed to have belonged to Africans or Afro-Brazilians repatriated after being flown back by diplomats Two skulls, including that of a man believed to have taken part in Brazil’s greatest slave revolt but whose remains were taken to the United States and used in racist eugenics studies at Harvard University, were repatriated on Wednesday.
The remains had been outside Brazil since the 19th century.

One was taken about 190 years ago from Salvador, the capital of the state of Bahia; the other, about 160 years ago, from Rio de Janeiro – and were welcomed back in moving, subdued ceremonies in both cities.

articles.title_zh: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
facts_zh:
Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike
- Published
Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.

Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas.
Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption.

all_titles.en: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike

articles.title_zh: African writing award probe finds 'no evidence' winning story was AI generated
facts_zh:
African writing award probe finds 'no evidence' winning story was AI generated
- Published
The Caine Prize for African Writing has said that after an internal review it has found no evidence that Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza had used generative AI to write his winning short story and confirmed him as the winner of this year's £10,000 ($13,000) award.

Ellah Wakatama, chair of the Caine Prize's board of trustees, said the matter had been investigated following an article in US magazine The Atlantic with the headline, Yet Another Literary Prizewinner Seems to Be AI.
"From our detailed investigation, we feel the evidence is clear: The Blue Fighter was human written," she said in a video posted on X.

all_titles.en: African writing award probe finds 'no evidence' winning story was AI generated

articles.title_zh: Ex-member of radical Marxist group scales balcony, escapes house arrest in Argentina
facts_zh: Leonardo Bertulazzi, 74, awaiting extradition to Italy, reportedly used harness to flee custody A 74-year-old former member of Italy ’s radical Marxist group the Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in Argentina , the country’s security ministry confirmed on Wednesday, after he reportedly hid his ankle monitor inside a tube of pork and lowered himself from a fifth-floor balcony.
Authorities placed Leonardo Bertulazzi under house arrest in Buenos Aires in 2024, prior to his extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence.
He had received the sentence in 1987 for joining a subversive association and belonging to an armed group.

- Published
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been moved from his Washington DC home to a military base after Iran-linked threats to his life, according to US media reports.
CBS, the BBC's US partner, said the relocation came after a photo of Bessent's home was published in the Wall Street Journal.

articles.title_zh: Indonesia's vice president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
facts_zh:
Indonesia's vice president resigns amid signs ruling alliance is fraying
- Published
Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has submitted his resignation, an aide has told the BBC, in a move which could further strain the political alliance that helped propel President Prabowo Subianto to power.
It comes after Indonesia's Supreme Court ruled that a high-school document used during Gibran's 2024 election campaign was invalid.
The ruling prompted more than 100 lawmakers to support a parliamentary initiative that could have paved the way for proceedings to impeach Gibran.

articles.title_original: Killing of journalist underscores deteriorating conditions in Ecuador
articles.title_zh: Killing of journalist underscores deteriorating conditions in Ecuador
facts_zh: Tomás Beltrán was shot dead amid gang warfare that has turned Latin American country into one of its most violent Tomás Beltrán was manoeuvring his car into his garage on Sunday night when the Ecuadorian journalist was shot dead.

Beltrán ran a Facebook page with news about Calceta, a small city in the province of Manabí, whose Pacific coastline has made it a key flashpoint in the gang warfare over drug trafficking routes that has transformed one of Latin America’s safest countries into one of its most violent .

articles.title_zh: Egyptian journalist's retrial adjourned as UN warns of 'assaults on press freedom'
facts_zh:
Egyptian journalist's retrial adjourned as UN warns of 'assaults on press freedom'
- Published
A criminal court in Cairo has postponed the retrial of the prominent Egyptian journalist Lina Attalah, whose case has drawn international condemnation.
Wednesday's opening hearing was adjourned until 18 November after defence lawyers representing the editor-in-chief of the news outlet Mada Masr requested a new judge.
The UN has warned of "widening assaults on press freedom by Egyptian authorities, including the targeting, persecution and harassment of independent journalists".

articles.title_original: Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter
articles.title_zh: Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter
facts_zh:
Four grizzly bears killed in Canada after fatal attack on mother and daughter
- Published
Four grizzly bears have been killed in connection with a fatal attack on a mother and daughter in the Canadian province of British Columbia.
Jennifer Balcarras, 48, and her daughter Selah Reed, 20, died earlier this month after going on an afternoon walk in a trail area in Bella Coola.
The British Columbia Conservation Office Service (BCCOS) launched an investigation into their deaths and forensic testing has since confirmed a sow and her three cubs were responsible for the attack.

articles.title_zh: Haitian PM praises El Salvador after joint strike on alleged home of gang leader
facts_zh:
Haitian PM praises El Salvador after joint strike on alleged home of gang leader
- Published
Haiti's Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé has praised "the commitment of the Salvadorean forces in the fight against gangs" after a joint strike on a house allegedly used by the leader of the 400 Mawozo gang.
El Salvador's President, Nayib Bukele, had earlier announced that a joint task force had "destroyed" what he described as "the house of Lanmò San Jou and the 400 Mawozo gang's headquarters".
A small contingent of Salvadorean troops has been in Haiti since January 2025 as part of a multinational force deployed to suppress gang violence.

articles.title_original: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth
articles.title_zh: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth
facts_zh:
US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth
- Published
An effort to impeach US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of waging war on Iran without congressional authorisation, has failed on Capitol Hill.

A majority of the House of Representatives voted to refer impeachment articles to a committee - essentially killing the effort introduced by dissident Republican congressman Thomas Massie of Kentucky.
During an earlier briefing, Hegseth called the impeachment effort a "farce" and "sabotage".

all_titles.en: US House blocks bid to impeach Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth

Transport workers in Chile block highways in protest over surging fuel prices
- Published
Hundreds of transport workers in Chile have blocked roads and highways across the country in protest over high fuel prices.
Drivers of busses and lorries began protesting on Tuesday, gathering in convoys to halt traffic along major routes.
They are demanding a relief from surging diesel prices, which have been driven up by the war in Iran.
